o.text: From Proto-Turkic *ak- (“to flow”). Cognate with Old Turkic [script needed] (ak-), Turkish akmak, Chuvash юх (juh).
Borrowed from Russian э́ра (éra), ultimately from Late Latin aera.

From Old Anatolian Turkish گرك (gäräk), ultimately from Proto-Turkic *kẹrge- (“need”), whence also Azerbaijani gərəkmək. Cognate with Old Turkic 𐰚𐰼𐰏𐰚 (kergek /⁠kr²gk⁠/).
Cognates
Bashkir кәрәк (käräk),
Turkmen gerek,
Tatar кирәк (kiräk),
Uyghur كېرەك (kërek),
Chuvash кирлӗ (kirlĕ),
Kazakh,
Kyrgyz,
Nogai,
Shor,
Karakalpak
Karachay-Balkar
Khakas, and
Kumyk керек (kerek),
Crimean Tatar and
Khalaj kerek,
Uzbek kerak,
Tuvan херек (xerek).
Compare also the Turkish verb Turkish gerekmek.
From Proto-Turkic *sïgïrčïk. Reshaped by addition of the suffix *-čin analogically to göyərçin.
From öz + -lə. Although the verb is archaic, today it also may be considered a reborrowing if used by speakers influenced by the Turkish language (cf. Turkish özlemek).
